title: Close the four non-deploy W4 follow-up items while SIT redeploy is running
lane: Claude Code - frontend verification, evidence, and cleanup follow-up
objective: Own the four remaining non-deploy W4 follow-up items in one staged pass while Copilot handles SIT deploy. Do real repo work, not only review: tighten Configurator evidence and wiring proof, improve focused regression coverage, align W4 status wording to the current repo truth, and either remove or explicitly document leftover dead-code / cleanup items.

four_work_items.name: Configurator and template-flow evidence hardening
four_work_items.intent: Treat TASK-1003, W4-04, and W4-05 as a combined repo-hardening pass: prove the 3-tab Configurator structure is not just shell markup, and tighten any missing wiring/evidence that can be completed safely in this pass.

four_work_items.name: Focused E2E or smoke pack expansion
four_work_items.intent: Improve the regression pack so it checks the current W4 shape more truthfully, especially around the 3-tab Configurator and the export wiring markers.

four_work_items.name: Doc and status alignment
four_work_items.intent: Update status wording so W4 docs reflect the current truth: SIT gate passed, checkbox close committed, Configurator shell landed, backend contract available, remaining work now about live proof and closure detail.

four_work_items.name: Dead code or explicit cleanup note
four_work_items.intent: Review the leftover orphaned Quick Export helper functions and either remove them if low-risk and truly unused, or document them explicitly as a non-blocking cleanup follow-up.

work_rules: Do not do SIT deploy, VPS changes, or control-plane workflow work. Copilot owns that lane.
Do not reopen the already accepted UX freeze debate unless you find a concrete repo-level contradiction.
Prefer repo-grounded implementation and focused verification over long narrative analysis.
If a cleanup is risky for this pass, document it clearly instead of forcing it into the same patch.
what_to_do: 1. Read W4-TASK-BOARD.md and map the four work items to the actual repo state before editing anything.
2. Inspect main-ux-ui.html and current tests to see which parts of the Configurator and export flow are structural only versus actually evidenced by tests or runtime markers.
3. Strengthen the Configurator follow-up where safe: tab-state behavior, apply-from-analysis flow, runtime summaries, preview/test-surface wiring, and template-flow evidence.
4. Expand tests/evidence so the W4 regression pack checks the current intended surface more truthfully than a DOM-only shell pass.
5. Update W4 docs/status wording to match the repo snapshot after this pass.

6. Review renderQuickPreview() and downloadQuickExportCsv() in main-ux-ui.html. If they are truly orphaned and removal is low-risk, delete them. If not, leave them and add a clear cleanup note in the relevant W4 doc.
7. Run focused verification for every code/doc change you make and report the exact result.
success_criteria: W4-03/04/05 evidence is stronger than before: the 3-tab Configurator and related flow are not described as 'not yet built' if the repo already contains them.
W4-09 regression coverage is improved with tests or equivalent proof that match the current W4 implementation shape.
W4-11 wording is aligned to the current repo state, not stale handoff assumptions.
The Quick Export orphaned-helper question is resolved either by cleanup or by explicit documented deferral.
Final answer states exactly what remains for Copilot SIT verification versus what is now complete locally.
